style=\"font-family:arial;\">\u003C/span>Lang Wedemeyer has helmed the Liberty's Women's Soccer team for eight seasons (2017-present), collecting an 89-46-20 record. Wedemeyer is a two-time Atlantic Sun Coach of the Year (2021, 22) and was selected as the VaSID Coach of the year in 2022. Wedemeyer and the Lady Flames secured their first-ever ASUN Championship title in the 2021 spring season. Two years later, he guided the team to the 2023 Conference USA Championship title in the team's debut season in the league. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWedemeyer came to Liberty following a highly successful 17-year run as the head women's soccer coach at South Dakota State. During his time at the helm of the Jackrabbits' program, Wedemeyer led South Dakota State to four Summit League championships and trips to the NCAA Women's Soccer Championship (2008, 2014, 2015 and 2016).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2024, the Lady Flames reached the CUSA Championship title game for the second time and the third conference title game (ASUN 2022) in as many years, but fell 1-0 to No. 1 seed and championship host, FIU. Wedemeyer guided the squad to a 15-2-4 record and secured a share of the CUSA Resgular Season title with a 6-1-2 CUSA mark. Liberty picked up a historic 2-1 victory at No. 21 Virginia Tech, securing the program's first victory over a ranked opponent. The Lady Flames also achieved its first-ever national ranking, slotting in at No. 24. Liberty received 10 selections to CUSA All-Conference teams including four first team honorees and three included on the All-Freshman team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn Liberty's debut season in Conference USA in 2023, Wedemeyer guided the Lady Flames to a 16-3-1 (5-2-1 CUSA) record and a CUSA title with a 2-1 victory in the championship final. The Lady Flames began the season with an 11-0 mark and a program-best 24-game unbeaten streak (dates back to 2022). Liberty secured a key 3-1 triumph over defending Big 12 champion West Virginia. Ainsley Leja (GK) and Rachel DeRuby (MF) received conference player of the year awards at their positions while eleven total Lady Flames received selection to CUSA All-Conference teams. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWedemeyer guided the Lady Flames to a conference best 14-3-4 record (8-0-2 ASUN) in 2022. Liberty's season came to an end in the ASUN Championship with the No.1 seed Lady Flames falling in penalty kicks 1-1 (3-4) to FGCU. In 2022, Wedemeyer was awarded with the United Soccer Coaches Association Faith Based Coach of the Year. Liberty was honored with nine ASUN All-Conference team members including the ASUN Goalkeeper of the Year, Ainsley Leja, in addition to four being named to the All-Freshman team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn the 2021 fall season, Wedemeyer led the Lady Flames to an 11-7-1 (6-3 ASUN). The Lady Flames' season ended in the ASUN Quarterfinals to Eastern Kentucky (1-0). Four Lady Flames earned All-Conference honors including Madison Ellis being selected to the first team. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWedemeyer and the Lady Flames secured their first ever ASUN Championship title in the 2021 spring season (moved from 2020 due to the COVID-19 Pandemic). Liberty earned a 7-6-5 record and topping four teams in the ASUN Championships including besting Kennesaw State 1-0 in OT to claim the title.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWedemeyer became State program in 2000 and guided the program through its transition to Division I in 2004. He has been honored for his coaching success, earning Summit League Coach of the Year honors in 2013 and 2014.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Additionally, he was named North Central Conference Coach of the Year in 2001 and South Dakota Sportswriters Women’s College Coach of the Year in 2008.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Wedemeyer has coached three Summit League Offensive Players of the Year and two Defensive Players of the Year. He also helped develop the skills of the 2012 Summit League Freshman of the Year.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Under his tutelage, 61 of Wedemeyer’s players have earned all-conference honors, including 27 first-team selections, 18 second-team honorees and 16 newcomers/freshman team members.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Wedemeyer’s teams have also had success in the classroom with his squads receiving the NSCAA Team Academic Award nine times (2006-07, 2009-14, 2016). Two of his former players have earned CoSIDA Academic All-America honors, while 10 players have earned CoSIDA All-District accolades. \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In addition to his 17 years of service at South Dakota State, Wedemeyer has worked with the National Soccer Coaches Association of America (NSCAA) as a national staff coach, conducting coaching certification and running clinics over the past 20 years.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>\u003Cstrong>Wedemeyer at a Glance\u003C/strong>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cul>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Played professionally for seven years.\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Wedeyemer has coached two All-Americans, 14 All-Region players, over 50 All-Conference players, eight Conference Players of the Year, and six players that have played professionally.\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Four Summit League Championships, five Summit League Regular Season Titles, four NCAA Tournament appearances and one Big South Regular Season Title (2017).\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>Coached nine ASUN All Conference Selections, two All-South Region Selections, eight Big South All-Conference Selections (Time at Liberty).\u003C/li>\r\n\t\u003Cli>187-148-44 Record\u003C/li>\r\n\u003C/ul>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Wedemeyer, a native of Roanoke, Va., began his collegiate playing career at Virginia Tech where he was voted the Hokies top defensive player in 1991 and 1992. He finished out his career at Old Dominion where he served as a team captain and was a 1994 CoSIDA Academic All-America second-team honoree.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Wedemeyer is married to Tabitha Wedemeyer. She primarily works with goalkeepers while contributing to the program as a whole.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn Collar's first season at Liberty, she helped lead Liberty to a 15-2-4 record (6-1-2 CUSA) and a finish as runners-up in the Conference USA Championship title game. Liberty picked up a historic 2-1 victory at No. 21 Virginia Tech, securing the program's first victory over a ranked opponent. Workman and Peyton Huber combined for 11 shutouts and a 0.62 GAA with 13 total goals allowed.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp class=\"MsoNormal\" style=\"text-align:justify;vertical-align:baseline\">\u003Cbr />\r\nCollar played a total of 13 games as a goalkeeper during her time at Liberty, making 27 saves.
